title: Lombards
capsule: The Lombards (Langobardi) were a Germanic people first attested along the lower Elbe who migrated southward through the 5th and early 6th centuries, settling in Pannonia by the early 500s, where they warred with the Gepids and built a kingdom under kings such as Wacho and Audoin. Under King Alboin they crushed the Gepids and in 568 invaded Italy, rapidly overrunning much of the peninsula and establishing a capital at Pavia, while leaving Ravenna, Rome, and the southern coast in Byzantine hands. After Alboin's murder (572) and a decade of rule by dukes, the monarchy was restored under Authari (r. 584-590), consolidating the young Lombard kingdom in northern Italy.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Lombard kingdom's core territories are well attested through legal and ecclesiastical records; the boundaries of the Lombard and Byzantine zones in Italy are documented with reasonable precision.
